title: Machine-Checked Exact-Rational Menu-Score, Knapsack Impossibility, and Bernstein Threshold-Guarantee Certificates for Downward-Closed Delegated Choice
abstract: Hamed Abdi, Kiarash Banihashem, MohammadTaghi Hajiaghayi, and Danny Mittal (arXiv:2611.33095, November 25, 2026) resolved two open frontiers in combinatorial delegated choice under downward-closed feasibility constraints: they designed a deterministic, agent-oblivious capped menu guaranteeing the principal strictly more than 29/70 (~0.41429) of the expected offline optimum V (Theorem 1.1, improving the previous 0.1098 bound), established a short analytic proof that a single reported-value threshold guarantees 3/10 (Theorem 4.1), and separated downward-closed constraints strictly from matroids (1/2) via a 5-item knapsack impossibility bounding every deterministic menu by 500/1011 (Proposition 3.1) and every randomized utility-aware rule by 30/61 (Theorem 3.2, Proposition 3.3; lowered to 0.48105 in Appendix A). We present a machine-checked, zero-floating-point formalization and exact-Q certificate auditor for the algebraic, combinatorial, Bernstein-positivity, and menu-score core of these results. First, an 18-theorem zero-dependency Lean 4 kernel (DownwardClosedDelegation.lean, Lean 4.35.0; 0 sorry, 0 warnings, 0 Classical.choice, 10 zero-axiom theorems) formalizes the 5-item knapsack optimum V=1011/50, sub-1/2 ratios 500/1011, 5011/10110, 30/61, normalized target R=7000000/2900007, constructive Lemma 2.1 best-response inclusion-maximality under positive agent utilities, Section 5 seed reserves b_P > 0, exact Section 4 Taylor (log(13/2) < 15/8) and small-b (168034/70785 > 0) positivity, universal positivity of P(b) > 0 over all rationals b in [2/13, 2/3] via exact homogeneous Bernstein expansion, and a general arbitrary-degree Bernstein convex lower bound. Second, DELEGATION-CERT-1.0 audits four exact-Q modes across 16 canonical certificates (0.050-1.077 ms) and rejects 60/60 live adversarial forgeries.
